$comment: contract-version 0.1.0 — initial idle-prompt digest contract (task #219, phase 1). Encodes the operator-ruled design SSOT (consolidated-idle-prompt-design v2 2026-07-07 + the three phase-1 provider docs): canonical envelope with band/age_band, assembler-computed hashing with post-on_included baselines, empty-sleep with header exclusion, size/trust/failure policies, second-person header, task-queue row shape, goal-state cadence, correlation rules.
title: Idle Prompt Digest Contract
description: SSOT JSON-Schema (draft 2020-12) for the consolidated idle-prompt digest. The SDK owns this SHAPE; the one canonical assembler IMPLEMENTATION lives in molecule_runtime and validates against these generated bindings — adapters only materialize the final prompt format. A workspace fires one non-empty, changed idle digest assembled from registered digest-provider plugins; every rendered section (identity header included) is a provider contribution. User prompts are NEVER digest contributions — they are synchronous top-priority input (operator ruling D3). Contributions are pull-not-dump envelopes; the assembler computes all delta hashes itself.

schema_version.description: Version of this idle-prompt contract layer.

contract_layer.description: SDK contract layer name, routable separately from workspace-comms/catalog/template layers.

providers.description: The official default-installed provider roster (settled order). Additional installed providers register through the same declaration shape at runtime; they are not listed here.

sample_contributions.description: Canonical contribution envelopes demonstrating the pinned header, an urgent task-queue envelope, a base task-queue envelope, and the goal-state cadence envelope.

ownership.description: The ruled shape-vs-engine split: the SDK owns the contract shape; the canonical assembler implementation lives in the workspace runtime.

shape_owner.description: This repo owns the contract shape and generated bindings.

assembler_owner.description: The one canonical assembler implementation lives in molecule-ai-workspace-runtime and validates against the generated bindings. No reimplement-per-runtime; adapters only materialize the final prompt format.

wakePolicy.description: Idle-fire policy. The idle-fire threshold is a SECOND consumer of the existing turn lease — one lease, two thresholds.

idle_fire_after_seconds.description: Silence window before the digest may fire (settled: 300). Test override permitted via runtime knob; the contract value is the production default.

stall_lease_is_separate.description: Load-bearing build gotcha: do NOT retune MOLECULE_TURN_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS (the stall knob, default pinned to the 900s idle-cap; the absolute turn cap defaults to 4x that TTL). The idle controller reads lease age + turn-in-flight state against its own threshold.

renew_on.description: Signals that renew the silence window (implicit keep-alive).

fire_preconditions.description: ALL must hold at injection time. Includes the atomic-fire recheck: immediately before injecting the KIND_IDLE turn, re-verify no-turn-in-flight AND no new inbound since assembly started; otherwise discard and reassemble next tick.

external_workspace_signal.description: External/BYO workspaces: platform-observable idleness is MCP-channel silence (weaker, accepted); the SDK owns a client-side lease and pulls the digest; a lease-renew ping suppresses firing during long local operations. Delivery != wake: offline agents receive the pending digest on reconnect.

sortPolicy.description: Render order (operator rulings D1/D2): pinned band first, then the urgent band above ALL base tiers, then base tiers ascending; tier-ordered within each band. NOT lexicographic (tier, urgency).

bands.description: The three render bands in order.

band.description: Render band. 'pinned' is a reserved capability grantable only to the official identity-capabilities provider; the assembler rejects any other provider declaring it.

ageBand.description: The ONLY time-derived field in hashed or rendered content — raw timestamps/durations are forbidden (a raw age changes every tick and resurrects the steady-state nag loop). Item ages use under-1h/1h-1d/over-1d; the goal cadence uses just-included/due; 'none' for time-free contributions (e.g. the header).

deltaPolicy.description: Delta gate: an unchanged digest never re-fires on a timer. ARMED (non-empty body): the idle timer keeps running, each tick re-assembles and fires only on hash change. SLEEPING (empty body): loop off, event-driven re-arm only.

hash_serialization.description: The canonical per-envelope serialization the ASSEMBLER hashes — the fixed tuple (provider_id, tier, urgency, count, summary, age_band, item_ids). 'band' is intentionally excluded: it is fully determined by provider_id (the reserved pinned id) and urgency, so it can neither change independently nor mask a re-fire. Providers cannot add hash inputs; anything that must re-fire the digest must be visible through these fields (e.g. item status serialized inside item ids as 'id:status').

provider_hash_role.description: A provider-supplied content hash is advisory at most: a buggy provider must not be able to mute itself with a constant hash nor re-fire every tick with a varying one.

baseline.description: Baselines are the hashes at the last successful fire, RECOMPUTED AFTER the on_included callbacks, then persisted in digest_state.json — so a band that resets on inclusion (goal cadence) is baselined at its post-reset value; baselining at fire-time values would deterministically double-fire one tick after every cadence fire. Ordering: stamp provider on_included state first, then persist baselines; a crash between the two costs at most one guard-governed extra turn.

stale_escalation_thresholds_seconds.description: Age-band boundaries: a stale item re-surfaces when it crosses a threshold (band transition = hash change), not every tick.

emptyPolicy.description: Empty => sleep. The pinned header never counts toward emptiness: a header-only digest is empty and must never fire.

rearm_events.description: In-process notification hooks that wake a SLEEPING controller (inbox handler, task-row writer, goal-state writer, provider registration, user-wake, config change).

scheduler_time_exception.description: The one permitted time-based re-arm: the controller records the scheduler provider's next-due timestamp and may sleep-until it. No other timer re-arms a sleeping controller.

limitsPolicy.description: Size bounds (test-overridable via runtime knobs; contract values are production defaults). The pinned header's capability lists are names-only.

truncation.description: Deterministic truncation when the digest budget is exceeded: drop preview detail from the lowest band/tier upward; counts and pull-instructions are never dropped.

failurePolicy.description: Provider failure semantics during assembly. A hung provider must never stall the tick.

on_error.description: Crash/timeout/malformed envelope => skip the section and render a one-line degraded marker.

failed_sections_excluded_from_hash.description: Crash/recover must not read as a content change and spuriously re-fire.

max_consecutive_failures.description: After K consecutive failures the provider is disabled and that fact surfaced once.

trustPolicy.description: Digest text lands directly in the agent's context — provider output is untrusted input.

reserved_provider_ids.description: Official ids the assembler rejects collisions/spoofing of.

third_party_default_tier.description: Additional installed providers default here (below scheduler, above goal) unless an operator-approved manifest grant declares otherwise.

urgency_grant.description: Third-party urgency requires an operator-approved manifest grant; official providers may declare per-envelope urgency.

pull_tools.description: Pull-instructions may reference whitelisted MCP tools only.

state_folder_jailing.description: Provider state paths are derived from the plugin name by the assembler, never provider-supplied; no provider writes another provider's folder.

callbackPolicy.description: After a successful fire the assembler notifies each provider whose contribution was included: on_included(fired_at). Consumers: goal-state cadence band; phase-2 sent-folder escalation timing. Providers may ignore it.

headerPolicy.description: The pinned identity/capabilities header render contract (operator ruling 2026-07-07): second person, persona/contract-derived, one source two renderings — never authored twice.

lines.description: Ordered rendered lines: you_are ('You are <name> — <persona role line>'), responsibility ('Your responsibility: ...'), priorities (generated from this contract's provider tier table, never authored), native_tools ('Your available MCP tools (native): ...').

native_tool_groups.description: Tool groups by origin, in render order.

platform_mcp_condition.description: The platform MCP group renders only when the workspace is the platform agent, derived from the actually-loaded mgmt-MCP inventory (not a declared flag); specialists never render it.

providerDecl.description: A digest-provider declaration. Official default-installed providers and additional installed providers use the same shape (installed plugins declare theirs via the plugin-manifest contributes surface).

base_tier.description: Base rank for non-urgent contributions; lower renders earlier within the base band. 0 for the pinned header (band overrides tier).

phase.description: Build phase: 1 = identity-capabilities, task-queue, goal-state; 2 = sent-folder, inbound-a2a, delegation-results, scheduler.

taskQueuePolicy.description: The task-queue provider (tier 1) — the durable work ledger where D3 user-pivot rows and lifecycle resume rows live. Platform requests/user_tasks stay authoritative for agent<->user asks (local rows index them); runtime-originated rows are locally authoritative.

store_owner.description: The store is runtime-owned, not provider-owned: it survives provider removal, so user-ask durability (operator-ruled D3) is never downgraded by removing a rendering lego.

single_current.description: At most one status='current' row, enforced by the writers' library.

envelopes.description: E1 urgent (open user-origin rows + open lifecycle resume rows) and E2 base tier 1 (current/paused/blocked/queued summary + awaiting-user asks).

urgent_open_definition.description: 'Open' for E1 = queued/paused/blocked; the current row is excluded (it renders in E2 only — no double-surface, one hash entry).

kernel_gated_writes.description: The whole D3 row-write + runtime-ack change is gated on MOLECULE_MAILBOX_KERNEL; flag-off is byte-identical legacy.

tombstone_retention_days.description: done/dropped rows kept as an idempotent re-index guard (the requests indexer must not zombie-re-upsert a locally-completed row while the platform row is still resolving) and for task_list history; absent from envelopes either way.

taskStatus.description: awaiting_user = requests-index rows (agent->user asks, origin='agent', request_id set); excluded from queued/current counts.

taskOrigin.description: 'a2a' and 'scheduler' are RESERVED for phase-2 writers. Task-row origin is orthogonal to turn source_type/kernel kinds: all lifecycle wake kinds write origin='lifecycle' rows.

taskRow.description: The durable task row. request_id indexes the platform requests/user_tasks lineage; delegation_id/correlation_id are nullable forward-links to phase-2 providers; resume_payload carries the lifecycle wake-up instruction written BEFORE any self-reprovision.

goalStatePolicy.description: The goal-state provider (lowest tier) — the loop. The cadence band is what keeps a static goal re-firing at its cadence under the delta gate instead of firing once and dying.

cadence_min_seconds.description: Cadence values below the idle-fire threshold are clamped.

cadence_band_rides_age_band.description: The provider reports its cadence band AS the envelope's age_band (just-included / due) and a goal-version id (hash of goal text + source) as its item id — every input flows through the assembler's existing hash tuple with zero kernel special-casing.

never_urgent.description: A background objective never jumps the queue.

migration_marker.description: Durable one-shot marker in the provider folder guarding the first-kernel-ON-boot migration. The migrator is the SINGLE writer of goal.yaml at migration time (the provisioner never writes the workspace volume); org-template-supplied values arrive already materialized as config.idle_prompt and migrate through this same path.

migration_overwrite_rule.description: Source-rank overwrite rule keeping precedence workspace-mcp > migrated-legacy > fleet-persona-default even when a provision default was written first.

goalDoc.description: The durable goal.yaml shape (goal_history.jsonl carries the append-only set/clear audit).

correlationPolicy.description: correlation_id rules (introduced by this contract — it does not exist in any repo today). Only sends with expects_reply=true write sent-folder rows; fire-and-forget messages never accumulate. Platform carriage (a2a_queue field + user-origin marker) is a molecule-core lane sequenced with this contract. SCOPE: this pins only the correlation PLUMBING (mint/echo/fallback/carry), which the design build-plan ratified. The bounce EMISSION and dead-recipient death-authority semantics (deleted vs failed vs paused) remain design-proposal P1, NOT operator-ruled, and are deliberately NOT pinned here. delegation_id single-minting-authority + echo rules are deferred to the phase-2 delegation providers (delegation_id appears here only as a nullable forward-link + reply fallback matcher).

fallback_matchers.description: Mixed-fleet reality: old-runtime/external/non-SDK recipients never echo correlation_id — without fallbacks every cross-version send becomes a permanently-escalating zombie row.

carried_by_bounce.description: The platform-emitted bounce envelope carries the original correlation_id so the sent-folder row closes deterministically.

lifecycleWakePolicy.description: Lifecycle wake-up calls (parent §5): one producer, typed-source-stamped so wakes are replay-guard-governed (today's initial_prompt/reprovision-wake stamp no source_type and bypass the guard).

resume_row_before_restart.description: The self-install tool durably writes the task-queue resume row BEFORE triggering reprovision — same invariant family as the delegation-tombstone commit-after-confirmed-delivery ordering.

contribution.description: The canonical contribution envelope. A provider MAY return multiple envelopes (item-level urgency per D2 — e.g. inbound-a2a lifts one urgent message into the band while the rest stays at base tier). The ASSEMBLER computes the delta hash over (provider_id, tier, urgency, count, summary, age_band, item_ids); 'band' is carried for rendering but excluded from the hash (it is derived from provider_id + urgency); advisory_content_hash is advisory at most.

urgency.description: 'urgent' lifts this envelope into the urgent band above ALL base tiers, including tier 1.

summary.description: Bounded rendered text (max_summary_bytes). Length/charset-constrained; treated as untrusted input.

item_ids.description: Stable provider-local item ids, serialized as 'id:status' where status changes must re-fire the digest. Empty for id-free contributions (e.g. the header).

advisory_content_hash.description: Optional provider-supplied hash — advisory at most; the assembler always computes its own.

rearm_signals.description: Provider-owned state transitions that re-arm a sleeping controller.

preview_items.description: Optional bounded preview rows (max_preview_items_per_envelope); full detail stays behind the pull instruction. Ages render as bands, never raw durations.

previewItem.description: A bounded preview row. NO raw time fields — age_band only.

pullInstruction.description: How the agent fetches bounded detail. 'tool' must be a whitelisted MCP tool (trust policy).
